newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa govt committee adopts tax incentives bill.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa govt committee adopts tax incentives bill.

text.p: The South African parliamentary finance committee on Monday paved the way for the introduction of tax incentives such as tax holidays by adopting the Revenue Laws Amendment Bill.
But Democratic Party finance spokesman Ken Andrew voted against the bill, which he said was "full of holes" and had been rushed through.
The bill enacts the tax holidays and accelerated depreciation allowances announced in June as part of the new macro-economic growth strategy.

They are due to come into effect on October 1 and there were fears that this deadline would not be met because of the limited time given to the committee to hear evidence on the bill before it was debated in parliament this week.
"Absolutely legitimate points raised by both labour and business haven't been addressed," Andrew said.

These included the possible impact of tax holidays on existing businesses, the limited time given to import plant machinery to qualify for accelerated depreciation allowance and the arbitrary discretion of the Minister of Finance to grant tax incentives.
"I just don't think that there have been adequate answers to these things and I think that the way that this is being rushed through is not good," Andrew said.

Other parties, including the African National Congress, said that they were satisfied with the answers provided by Deputy Finance Minister Gill Marcus and Department of Trade and Industry chief director Alan Hirsch.

But the committee, which said its public hearings last week had "provided valuable insight to the issues" in the bill, decided to forward all the submissions received to Finance Minister Trevor Manuel "for his consideration".
Technically, the committee can only accept or reject the "money" bill.
